newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Hostage-taker Basayev resigns as Chechen deputy PM.
newsitem.headline: Hostage-taker Basayev resigns as Chechen deputy PM.

text.p: Former Chechen field commander Shamil Basayev, who led a daring hostage-taking raid on a Russian town in 1995, said on Thursday he had resigned as a deputy prime minister of the separatist region.

"I have resigned of my own accord," Basayev told Reuters by telephone. He did not elaborate and there was no official announcement from Chechen President and Prime Minister Aslan Maskhadov, who named Basayev his deputy in April.
Basayev, born in 1965, lost to Maskhadov in a presidential election in January. There have been media reports about frictions between the two most popular men in Chechnya which both have denied.
Basayev was one of the most radical field commanders who fought Russian troops trying to quell Chechnya's independence drive in a 1994-1996 war in which tens of thousands died.

He became a national hero in Chechnya and a figure of hate in Moscow in June 1995 when he and his guerrilla fighters sneaked out of Chechnya and stormed the southern Russian town of Budennovsk taking more than 1,000 hostages in a local hospital.
More than 100 people were killed and Basayev returned to Chechnya with his group.
The brash act forced Moscow to start talks, but a realistic truce was signed only in August 1996 and a formal peace deal last May.
